Today's Featured Research Reports

Intel's shares have outperformed the Zacks Semiconductor - General industry over the year-to-date period (+137.5% vs. +19.8%). The company is likely to be plagued by memory and supply constraints, intense competition and exposure to China. Foundry adoption remains dependent on execution, while heavy investment and uneven cash generation constrain flexibility. The stock's elevated valuation leaves limited room for setbacks. 

However, Intel's manufacturing recovery and expanding AI portfolio support a broader growth profile across client, data center and foundry markets. Server demand, AI PCs, purpose-built silicon and advanced packaging are widening customer engagement, while the 18A roadmap is moving through risk production and high-volume manufacturing milestones. 

Intel's local AI strategy also has a practical enterprise use case, with Arizona State University deployment showing potential productivity gains from on-device agents and vPro security.

(You can read the full research report on Intel here >>>)

Shares of Novartis have gained +13.7% over the year-to-date period against the Zacks Large Cap Pharmaceuticals industry's gain of +19.4%. The company's recent performance demonstrated that its portfolio of newer growth products is increasingly capable of offsetting the impact of generic competition, including the loss of U.S. exclusivity for blockbuster heart failure drug Entresto. 

Generic competition for Promacta is also pulling down the top line. The company has a strong and diverse portfolio, with key drugs like Kisqali, Kesimpta, Pluvicto and Leqvio. Our model estimates for Pluvicto and Kisqali indicate a CAGR of 26.8% and 26.2%, respectively, over the next three years. 

Novartis is also strengthening its long-term growth outlook through targeted business development.  Key upcoming catalysts across various pipeline programs are positioned to support mid-term growth outlook. However, recent pipeline setbacks have dampened investor sentiment.

(You can read the full research report on Novartis here >>>)

Itau Unibanco's shares have gained +9% over the year-to-date period against the Zacks Banks - Foreign industry's gain of +13.1%. The company's earnings met the estimates in one of the trailing four quarters. The conditional approval for a Miami-based national bank will expand its U.S. wealth-management capabilities, while strategic buyouts continue to strengthen its digital and investment businesses. 

Steady revenue growth is supported by strong insurance, asset management and investment banking operations. Also, solid funding should help maintain a healthy credit portfolio. 

However, the company's expenses are expected to remain elevated due to higher technology investments, despite cost-control efforts. Any economic slowdown in Brazil or Latin America could hurt its operational efficiency and profitability. Weakening credit quality amid the volatile macroeconomic environment remains a concern.

(You can read the full research report on Itau Unibanco here >>>)

Shares of AMREP have outperformed the Zacks Real Estate - Development industry over the year-to-date period (+12.4% vs. -29.4%). This microcap company with a market capitalization of $111.45 million has an extensive land bank, expanding homebuilding operations and growing rental portfolio to support its long-term growth prospects. A healthy homebuilding pipeline, flexible development strategy and strong liquidity position provide opportunities for sustained growth. 

However, weak land sales, housing affordability challenges, limited contracted backlog and rising administrative costs remain concerns. Customer and geographic concentration, margin pressures and slower capital recycling further add to operating risks. 

The stock's valuation suggests potential upside for investors, supported by its asset base and long-term growth opportunities. However, persistent market uncertainties and uneven operating performance could limit near-term gains. Investors may prefer a cautious approach until demand conditions stabilize and earnings visibility improves.

(You can read the full research report on AMREP here >>>)

Red Hat Pays IBM's Bills While Xeon Outruns Intel's Factories

IBM's revenue rose 4.7% to $17.10 billion. The growth rate is low, so the mix matters more. Software reached $7.80 billion, Red Hat grew 11%, and OpenShift is now a $2.4 billion ARR business. Enterprises renew that kind of revenue as they update their apps for AI. IBM Z mainframe sales fell 20%, but Distributed Infrastructure grew 31% and made up for it. Arvind Krishna credited "disciplined execution" for the faster growth.

Intel's growth was far more dramatic. Revenue rose 25.4% to $16.13 billion, and Data Center and AI revenue jumped 59%. Lip-Bu Tan called it the "strongest revenue growth in more than fifteen years." Foundry results fell behind. Intel Foundry lost $2.1 billion, and external foundry revenue was only $293 million. A $12.53 billion CHIPS Act escrow charge also pushed Intel to a GAAP net loss of $11.0 billion.

title: Intel Gains 4% on New Street Upgrade as Server CPU Crunch Is Set to “Persist for Years”

Trading disclosure
Intel Gains 4% on New Street Upgrade as Server CPU Crunch Is Set to "Persist for Years" ©Dean Drobot and Nikada from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Intel shares rose 4% today after New Street Research upgraded the stock to Buy from Neutral with a $125 price target.

New Street argues that AI agents will keep server CPUs in short supply for years, and Intel's own data center results back up that demand.

New Street's 2030 earnings forecast is only a little above Wall Street's, so the target mostly needs the current consensus to hold.

Intel reports third-quarter results on Thursday, Oct. 29, and the data center margin is the number to watch.

Intel (INTC:NASDAQ) stock rose 4% today after New Street Research upgraded the chipmaker to Buy from Neutral with a $125 price target before the open.

Analyst Pierre Ferragu's case is all about server chips:

"Agentic AI is driving a sustained increase in server CPU demand, with supply constraints set to persist for years, while Intel is getting rid of bad nodes and adding capacity," he wrote.

The shortage is already in Intel's numbers

New Street estimates Intel's server capacity can grow more than 50% in 2027. By 2030, it sees $50 billion of server CPU revenue for Intel, even as Intel's share of a market topping $220 billion slips to 20% to 25%.

Intel's own results back up the demand. Data Center and AI revenue jumped 59% to $6.3 billion in the second quarter, and the segment's operating margin hit 39.5%, up from 16.1% a year earlier.

Some of that is pricing, though. Server prices fell 4% in 2025 before Intel raised them during this year's shortage, and those margins could slip once supply loosens.

TIKR tracks 50 analysts on Intel. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Intel, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Intel's Analyst Ratings

The target leans on Wall Street's own math

New Street's target rests on its forecast of $7.10 in EPS for 2030. That's only a bit above the $6.59 consensus for that year, and the consensus path is already steep…

Intel (INTC): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023–2028 (TIKR)

New Street thinks a data center beat could lift those estimates next year. And its $125 target isn't far from the $117 consensus.

The price is the harder part. Intel traded at 51x forward earnings at the last close…

Intel (INTC): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

That's right at its five-year average of 50x, but years of tiny earnings inflate that average (the multiple hit 173x a year ago). From 2014 to 2022, Intel traded between 10x and 18x.

Thursday is the first test

Intel reports third-quarter results on Thursday, Oct. 29, after the close. Management guided for $15.8 billion to $16.8 billion of revenue, a 42% non-GAAP gross margin and $0.38 of non-GAAP EPS. Intel has topped its own guidance seven quarters running.

title: Intel and TSMC Are Vying for Chip Fabrication Supremacy. 1 Offers Superior Value.
detail:
Intel and TSMC Are Vying for Chip Fabrication Supremacy. 1 Offers Superior Value.
Keithen Drury, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 11:05 AM EDT 4 min read
INTC
TSM
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) (NYSE: TSM) and Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) are two major names in the chip fabrication world. However, Taiwan Semiconductor has a monster lead that cannot be overstated. Intel used to be a major player, but because it let its technology slip, clients gradually moved their business to other foundries, namely TSMC.

However, with recent investments from Nvidia and the U.S. government, Intel's chip foundry business looks to be back in action. There is a major market shift that could happen over the next few years, but which stock is best positioned to capitalize on it? Let's take a look.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
Intel is seeing strong growth

Intel splits its business into two parts: Intel Foundry and Intel Products. Intel products include the devices that it makes, like CPUs, and it is split into two divisions: Client Computing and the Physical AI Group, and Data Center and AI. This is not what's coming against TSMC, but it is doing pretty good growth figures, with revenue rising 28% year over year to $15.1 billion. Still, it's good to know in the context of Intel as a whole, as an investment in Intel also acquires these segments, not just its foundry business.

Intel's foundry business has steadily improved and generated revenue of $5.8 billion, up 31% year over year. So, it's a lot smaller of a business unit than its products. However, if Intel's foundry business can continue acquiring clients, this could be the start of a major growth trend.

However, it's much smaller in size than TSMC. TSMC is only a foundry company, so it should only be compared to that division from Intel. In Q3, its revenue totaled $46.7 billion, up 41% year over year. We're still waiting on Intel's Q3 results, so if we rewind the clock to Q2, TSMC grew at a 34% year over year pace to $40.2 billion.

So, if Q2 results are used, TSMC and Intel are about on the same level in terms of growth, although TSMC has a notable size advantage.

But there is one glaring difference that investors cannot miss: profitability. Right now, Intel is fighting to get its foundry business back to profitability. In Q2, its operating margin was a pretty sad 36% loss. On the flip side, TSMC's operating profit margin was 59%.

So, Intel's Foundry business is currently a major loss leader for the company, while TSMC has achieved an incredible level. I think this is something notable to keep in mind, as it helps put the valuation of the two in context.
